data.title: Two plans for one corner

memoryNodes.cue: Two plans conflict over the same space.
memoryNodes.cueZh: 两种计划争用同一个空间。

memoryNodes.cue: Jo helps the groups find an arrangement.
The groups reach a friendly agreement.

data.situation:
At eleven, the afternoon organisers gathered by the window. One group wanted a quiet conversation in that corner; another wanted music there. Their views clashed, and the discussion became sharp. Jo stepped in before either group began moving the chairs. She offered to mediate, asking each organiser to explain what mattered most. Then she drew two possible arrangements on the room plan. Jo: Let us work out where each group can go.
Music organiser: I am angry because we were promised this space.
Jo: I understand. I cannot placate you with another promise I may not be able to keep. Let us check the larger room together.
Conversation organiser: If music goes there, we can stay by the window.
By the time they returned, they had reached an amicable agreement. Room update
Music: main hall.
Conversation: window corner.
Both organisers have agreed to the change. Please use the new room plan.

readingBlocks.en: At eleven, the afternoon organisers gathered by the window. One group wanted a quiet conversation in that corner; another wanted music there. Their views clashed, and the discussion became sharp. Jo stepped in before either group began moving the chairs. She offered to mediate, asking each organiser to explain what mattered most. Then she drew two possible arrangements on the room plan.
readingBlocks.zh: 十一点，下午活动的组织者聚到窗边。一组想在那个角落安静交谈，另一组想在那里放音乐。他们的意见发生冲突，讨论变得尖锐。在任何一组开始搬椅子前，乔介入了。她提出调解，请双方各自解释最重要的需求，随后在房间图上画了两种可能的安排。

readingBlocks.en:
Jo: Let us work out where each group can go.
Music organiser: I am angry because we were promised this space.
Jo: I understand. I cannot placate you with another promise I may not be able to keep. Let us check the larger room together.
Conversation organiser: If music goes there, we can stay by the window.
By the time they returned, they had reached an amicable agreement.
readingBlocks.zh:
乔：我们一起想办法，确定每组能去哪里。
音乐活动组织者：我生气，是因为有人答应把这个地方给我们。
乔：我理解。我不能再用一个未必能兑现的承诺来安抚你。一起去看看大房间吧。
谈话活动组织者：如果音乐活动搬去那里，我们就留在窗边。
他们回来时，已经友好地达成协议。

glossary.note: 动词，clash over something/clash with；不是碰撞或颜色不协调。
glossary.example: Their views clashed over the use of the corner.
glossary.exampleZh: 他们对角落用途的意见发生冲突。

glossary.note: step in to help/mediate；过去式stepped in。
glossary.example: Jo stepped in when the discussion became sharp.
glossary.exampleZh: 讨论变尖锐时，乔介入了。

externalEvidence.definition: get involved, so as to alter or hinder an action, or through force or threat of force

glossary.note: mediate between A and B；不是自行替双方作决定。
glossary.example: Jo offered to mediate between the two groups.
glossary.exampleZh: 乔提出在两组之间调解。

externalEvidence.definition: act between parties with a view to reconciling differences

glossary.zh: 通过思考或讨论解决；想出办法
glossary.note: work out a solution/what to do；不是锻炼身体。
glossary.example: They worked out where each group could go.
glossary.exampleZh: 他们商量出每组能去哪里。

externalEvidence.definition: find the solution to (a problem or question) or understand the meaning of

glossary.zh: 使生气或不满的人平静下来；安抚
glossary.note: placate someone；较正式，突出平息愤怒，不表示问题必已解决。
glossary.example: Jo refused to make a false promise just to placate the organiser.
glossary.exampleZh: 乔不肯只为安抚组织者而作虚假承诺。

externalEvidence.definition: cause to be more favorably inclined; gain the good will of

glossary.note: 常形容协议、关系或解决过程；与amiable性情友好区分。

externalEvidence.definition: characterized by friendship and good will
